subsystem: packages/web — console design system: tokens, primitives, shell (not screens)
summary: A terminal/control-plane design system built on exactly one CSS file, 21 stock shadcn/ui primitives and 6 bespoke components. The single idea that makes it leaner than mcphub: every color is a semantic token that swaps itself, so the `dark:` variant is banned in application code — mcphub's 284 `!important` declarations and 1000+ raw `text-gray-700` utilities exist because it had `--hub-*` tokens for some things and Tailwind palette colors for the rest, then had to retrofit the difference. Here `@theme inline` defines both our tokens and every name shadcn emits (`--color-card`, `--color-muted-foreground`, `--color-ring`, …), so the undefined-class bug at mcphub LogViewer.tsx:70,148,160 is structurally impossible and a 40-line vitest proves it each build. All 16 palette values are measured: every status color and ink-3 clears WCAG AA 4.5:1 against all four background layers in both themes, and `--line-strong` clears 3:1 as a control border — four values failed on the first pass and were fixed, listed in the contrast ledger. The identifier rule (mono + tabular for every tool name, server name, endpoint, id and token count) is carried by one `<Id>` component and one 22-line ESLint rule, not by discipline.
phase: Phase 1 — foundation. Lands before any screen work; the screen/data agent consumes `@/ui/*`, `@/shell/*` and the command registry as given. No screen may add a color, a radius, a duration or a font size.

decisions.decision: `:root` holds the DARK values; light is `[data-theme="light"]`. The `dark:` variant is an ESLint error in application code.
decisions.rationale: Dark-first means dark is literally the default cascade, not a class you add. If a component needs `dark:` to look right, a semantic token is missing — that is the rule that stops the retrofit layer before it starts.
decisions.cost: One `@custom-variant light` for the two places (illustrations, syntax-highlight theme) that genuinely differ beyond a token swap.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: mcphub's `@custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark,.dark *))` plus ~900 lines of `.dark .text-gray-700 { … !important }` retrofit at index.css:470-1385.

decisions.decision: `@theme inline` defines our 16 tokens AND aliases every name shadcn/ui emits onto them. A vitest asserts each contract name resolves to a non-empty computed value.
decisions.rationale: `@theme inline` emits `var(--x)` into the generated utilities instead of copying the value, so one `[data-theme]` override reaches every shadcn component. The test is the mechanical guard that an undefined utility can never ship silently.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: mcphub claimed shadcn but installed only `@radix-ui/react-slot`; `bg-card` and `text-muted-foreground` in LogViewer.tsx:70,148,160 were undefined no-op classes nobody noticed.

decisions.decision: The brand color token is `--color-brand`. shadcn's `--color-accent` is mapped to our neutral `--surface`, not to the brand.
decisions.rationale: In shadcn's vocabulary `accent` means "subtle hover surface" and is emitted by every dropdown item, command item and calendar day. Mapping a saturated cyan there turns every menu hover into a cyan block, and the fix people reach for is `!important`.
decisions.cost: One naming divergence from shadcn docs, documented at the top of theme.css.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: n/a — mcphub never installed enough of shadcn to hit this collision, which is why it never learned it.

decisions.decision: Geist Sans + Geist Mono self-hosted from the pinned `geist` 1.7.2 package, two variable woff2 files, `font-display: optional` + `<link rel=preload>`. No metric-override fallback face.
decisions.rationale: `optional` is the only `font-display` value that guarantees both zero FOUT and zero layout shift — the browser either uses the font from first paint or not at all for that load, so there is no mid-page swap for a fallback face to smooth over. Vite fingerprints the files, so every visit after the first is Geist.
decisions.cost: A cold first visit on a slow link paints in system sans/mono. Acceptable: the fallback stack is also mono, so identifiers stay monospaced.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: mcphub declared Geist Mono and JetBrains Mono in CSS but bundled neither, so every install silently rendered system fallback.

decisions.decision: The identifier rule is enforced by one `<Id kind=…>` component plus a 22-line local ESLint rule `mcprouter/no-bare-identifier`, not by review.
decisions.rationale: The rule flags any JSX child expression ending in `name`/`url`/`id`/`tokens`/`latencyMs`/… unless its parent element is ``, so a raw `{tool.name}` fails CI. Because `body` is Geist Sans, a violation that somehow lands is also visibly wrong next to its `` siblings.
decisions.cost: One local ESLint plugin file; the rule needs its property-name regex extended when the data layer adds a field.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: mcphub had no identifier convention at all — tool names render in whatever the surrounding card used.

decisions.decision: The inspector is one URL search param (`?inspect=server:github`). Stacking is impossible by construction. Only `alert-dialog` may layer on top, only for destructive confirms.
decisions.rationale: One param can hold one value, so there is no stack to mismanage, and every inspector state is linkable and survives the back button. Docked ≥1280px (non-modal, page stays usable), `<Sheet>` below that (Radix focus-trapped).
decisions.cost: Deep inspector→inspector navigation replaces rather than pushes; a breadcrumb in the inspector header covers it.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: mcphub's ServerForm.tsx is a single 2300-line modal, and ActivityPage uses native `window.confirm`/`alert()` for results.

decisions.decision: The nav rail and the cmdk palette render from the same `registry.ts` array. A route that is not in the array is not in the nav and not in the palette.
decisions.rationale: Two hand-maintained lists drift within a month; one array cannot. Dynamic entries (servers, groups, tools) come from the same TanStack Query caches the screens use, so the palette is never stale.
decisions.cost: Registry entries carry an `icon`, a `shortcut` and a `keywords` array they would not otherwise need.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: mcphub has no palette and no keyboard shortcuts anywhere; SettingsPage.tsx is 3928 lines of accordion with no search and no deep link.

decisions.decision: Do not install shadcn `scroll-area`. Style native scrollbars in `@layer base` instead.
decisions.rationale: Radix ScrollArea replaces native scrolling with a transform, which breaks CSS scroll-anchoring and list virtualization — exactly what the log firehose and the activity table need. Eight lines of `::-webkit-scrollbar` + `scrollbar-width: thin` gets the same look with none of that.
decisions.cost: Scrollbar styling differs slightly between Firefox and Chromium. Nobody will notice.
decisions.mcphub_contrast: mcphub's LogViewer renders every entry from an unbounded array with no virtualization; keeping native scroll is what makes fixing that a one-library change later.

decisions.decision: No inline theme-boot script in index.html. Dark is the default cascade, so it needs no JavaScript; the stored *light* preference is applied from the main bundle.
decisions.rationale: This keeps CSP at a clean `script-src 'self'` with no hash plumbing and no `'unsafe-inline'`. The cost falls only on users who explicitly chose light: one frame of dark on first paint.
decisions.cost: One-frame flash for light-theme users on a cold load. `ponytail: acceptable for a self-hosted console; move to an inline script with a vite-computed CSP hash if anyone complains.

interfaces.name: packages/web/src/styles/theme.css — the whole design system, one file
interfaces.notes: ~180 lines, the only stylesheet in the package. Contains exactly 3 `!important` declarations, all inside the reduced-motion block; a 6-line vitest asserts that count so the mcphub retrofit layer cannot grow here. Every oklch value below is in sRGB gamut (verified) so the rendered color is the specified color, not a browser gamut-map of it.

interfaces.name: Contrast ledger — measured, not estimated
interfaces.notes: Computed by oklch→OKLab→linear sRGB→relative luminance→(L1+0.05)/(L2+0.05). Ratios are against all four background layers; the column shown is the MINIMUM across bg #0a0c0f / raised #131619 / sunken #050608 / surface #1e2124 (dark) and #f9fafb / #ffffff / #eef0f3 / #f4f5f7 (light). The minimum is always against `--surface` in dark and `--sunken` in light. AA text = 4.5:1, AA non-text/UI = 3:1.

DARK                                   LIGHT

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  dark  9.45:1 vs bg · 8.78:1 vs raised · 7.84:1 vs surface   -> PASS 3:1

FIVE VALUES FAILED ON THE FIRST PASS AND WERE CHANGED:
1. dark brand oklch(0.76 0.135 205) and dark busy oklch(0.75 0.13 265) were
   OUT OF sRGB GAMUT — the browser clamped them to #00c9da / #85acff, so the
   shipped color was not the specified one. Chroma cut 0.135->0.100 and
   0.13->0.100. Same fix for light warn (0.12->0.095) and light brand (0.13->0.110).
2. dark idle at L 0.62 measured 4.46:1 on --surface. FAILED AA text by 0.04.
   Raised to L 0.66 -> 5.22:1.
3. light idle at L 0.55 measured 4.25:1 on --sunken. FAILED. Darkened to
   L 0.50 -> 5.26:1.
4. --line-strong at L 0.42 (dark) / L 0.80 (light) measured 2.15-2.31 and
   1.79-1.87. FAILED the 3:1 rule for interactive control borders (WCAG 1.4.11).
   Moved to L 0.55 / L 0.62 -> 3.35 / 3.19 minimum.
5. The usual neon failure is avoided by not going neon: ok sits at L 0.79
   rather than a 0.88 phosphor green (which loses contrast against --surface
   only marginally but reads as a toy), and err is LIGHTENED to L 0.72 rather
   than kept at a conventional saturated mid red, because a mid red clears 4.5:1
   on #0a0c0f and then fails on #1e2124 where most err text actually sits.

NON-COLOR REDUNDANCY: no state is signalled by hue alone. <StatusDot> carries a
distinct glyph per state, and every status in a table is accompanied by its word.

interfaces.name: packages/web/src/ui/id.tsx — THE identifier rule, enforced
interfaces.notes: ~115 lines. The single place `.id` may be applied. `kind='tool'` needs an explicit `server` prop to split the `<server><sep><tool>` namespace (mcphub normalizeToolForCache mcpService.ts:638, separator from getNameSeparator() default '-', config/index.ts:256) — splitting on the last separator is a heuristic that breaks on tool names containing the separator, so it is not done.

interfaces.name: packages/web/eslint-local/no-bare-identifier.js — what stops a raw <span>
interfaces.notes: 22 lines. Registered as `mcprouter/no-bare-identifier` at error level for `src/**/*.tsx`. This is the enforcement; the mono-vs-sans visual difference is only the backup that makes a violation obvious in review. Extend ID_PROP when the data layer adds a field — that is the one maintenance cost.

interfaces.name: packages/web/src/shell/app-shell.tsx — the layout shell
interfaces.notes: ~120 lines for the shell itself; NavRail/Topbar/StatusBar/Inspector add ~200. One search param owns the inspector, so a stack cannot form (D6). The four CSS custom properties set here are the only sanctioned inline style in the codebase.

interfaces.name: Keyboard shortcut map + useHotkeys
interfaces.notes: One `keydown` listener in AppShell, ~50 lines, zero dependencies — no react-hotkeys-hook. Guards `e.isComposing` (IME), editable targets, and lets cmdk own its own keys while open. Every shortcut is also a palette entry, so none of them is hidden knowledge. `?` opens the cheatsheet, which renders this same table from the registry.

interfaces.name: cmdk command palette — registry and reach
interfaces.notes: ~220 lines including the registry. Static actions live in one array; dynamic entries read the same TanStack Query caches the screens use, so the palette can never show a stale server list. Settings sections are registered individually — this is what makes them deep-linkable, which mcphub's 3928-line SettingsPage.tsx with 11 accordions and no search cannot do.

interfaces.name: Component inventory
interfaces.notes: 21 stock shadcn primitives + 6 bespoke. Installed with `pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add …` into `src/ui/` (not `src/components/ui/` — shorter import path, same thing). The generated files are edited in place when needed; nothing is re-skinned from outside with overrides, which is the mechanism that keeps `!important` at three.
interfaces.sketch:
INSTALLED AS-IS (16) — used exactly as generated, zero wrappers
  button        cva extended with size="xs" (24px) and variant="quiet";
                edited IN the generated file, never overridden from outside
  input · textarea · label · select · checkbox · separator · skeleton
  badge         variants extended: ok | warn | err | idle | busy -> .tint-* classes
  collapsible · popover · dropdown-menu · tabs · table · alert-dialog · sonner

  switch        UNWRAPPED, and this is the point: Radix Switch already emits
                role="switch" + aria-checked + full keyboard. mcphub hand-rolled
                .hub-switch on a plain <button> with neither. The reason to wrap
                no longer exists.

WRAPPED (5) — each wrapper justified by something it removes, not adds
  tooltip   -> <Tip>            hoists one <TooltipProvider delayDuration={200}>
                                and collapses 4 lines of Trigger/Content boilerplate
                                per use. ~60 call sites.
  dialog    -> (unwrapped)      used directly for confirm-free forms
  sheet     -> <Inspector>      the responsive half of D6: same children render
                                docked >=1280 and as a Sheet below
  command   -> <CommandPalette> needs the global hotkey + the registry
  switch    -> <StateSwitch>    adds `pending`: aria-busy, disabled, busy-colored
                                thumb. Every switch here mutates a live server,
                                so pending is not optional.

NOT INSTALLED — deliberate
  scroll-area   breaks scroll anchoring + virtualization for the log firehose (D8);
                native scrollbars are styled in @layer base instead
  form          zod 4.6.5 + uncontrolled inputs; react-hook-form is the data
                agent's call, not the design system's
  radio-group · avatar · accordion · carousel · chart

BESPOKE (6) — nothing in Radix or shadcn covers these
  <Id>          the identifier rule. see its own entry. ~115 loc.
  <StatusDot>   6 states, each with a DISTINCT GLYPH so state never depends on
                hue alone: ok ● / warn ▲ / err ✕ / idle ○ / busy ◐ (CSS spin,
                static under reduced-motion) / sleeping ◌ (startOnDemand servers).
                role="img" + aria-label="connected" etc. ~50 loc.
                Replaces mcphub's literal emoji at StatusDot.tsx:67,83.
  <LogLine>     fixed 20px row: level gutter (2px color bar) | ts (2xs mono) |
                server <Id> | message. Text nodes ONLY, never
                dangerouslySetInnerHTML; ANSI stripped by one regex rather than
                an ansi-to-html dependency — which closes an injection class for
                free. Click expands the payload into the inspector. ~70 loc.
  <Sparkline>   inline <svg>, up to 60 points, one <polyline>, preserveAspectRatio
                none. No charting library for a 72x20 box. role="img" with an
                aria-label carrying min/max/last as text. ~40 loc.
  <CostBar>     stacked horizontal bar: gross vs exposed tokens per server/group,
                plus the Smart-Routing meta-tool cost with and without Progressive
                Disclosure so the saving is visible. role="img" + textual label;
                the numbers are also printed as <Id kind="tokens">. ~45 loc.
  <ToolTree>    tri-state checkbox tree for per-server tool/prompt/resource
                selection inside a group. Radix has no tree primitive.
                role="tree"/"group"/"treeitem", aria-checked="mixed" on partial
                parents, aria-expanded, roving tabindex, Left/Right collapse-expand.
                Shows <Id kind="tokens"> per node. ~130 loc.

WHAT CONCRETELY PREVENTS THE MCPHUB OUTCOME
  1. @theme inline defines every shadcn contract name; theme.contract.test.ts
     fails the build if one resolves empty. (mcphub: bg-card / text-muted-foreground
     undefined at LogViewer.tsx:70,148,160.)
  2. ESLint bans the Tailwind palette, `dark:`, inline style, and literal colors
     in class names. (mcphub: 1000+ raw text-gray-700 / bg-gray-800.)
  3. theme.lint.test.ts pins !important at exactly 3, all in the reduced-motion
     block. (mcphub: 284 occurrences across index.css:470-1385.)
  4. No tailwind.config.js and no postcss.config.js exist. (mcphub kept both as
     dead v3 files beside its v4 setup.)
  5. `geist` is a real dependency and theme.css imports the woff2 by path, so a
     wrong path fails the Vite build. (mcphub declared fonts it never bundled.)
  6. Variants go INTO the generated cva, never into an override stylesheet.

interfaces.name: Accessibility floor
interfaces.notes: Non-negotiable; part of the definition of done for every screen the other agent builds. Radix supplies most of it, which is the argument for actually installing shadcn rather than claiming it.
interfaces.sketch:
CONTROLS
  switch        Radix role="switch" + aria-checked, free. <StateSwitch> adds
                aria-busy during a mutation. Always paired with a VISIBLE
                <Label htmlFor>; never a bare icon.
  status        <StatusDot role="img" aria-label="connected">. Distinct glyph per
                state, so the information survives grayscale and every form of CBU.
                Every table that shows a dot also shows the word.
  dot as button when clickable (oauth_required -> authorize), it becomes a real
                <button> with a 24x24 hit box (WCAG 2.2 AA 2.5.8) and its own label.
  bulk select   checkbox column has an aria-label naming the row's subject.

FOCUS
  one ring      2px solid --brand, offset 2px, from a single :focus-visible rule in
                @layer base. Measured >=4.74:1 against every layer in both themes.
                Offset puts it outside brand-filled buttons so it never vanishes.
  trapping      Dialog / AlertDialog / Sheet / CommandDialog = Radix, trapped,
                aria-modal, Esc, scroll-lock, focus restored on close. Nothing is
                hand-rolled. (mcphub's hand-built modals have no trap.)
  not trapped   the DOCKED inspector is intentionally non-modal:
                role="complementary" + aria-label, reachable by Tab, closed by Esc
                when it holds focus.
  skip link     first focusable node in the DOM, -> #main (tabIndex={-1}).
  roving        ToolTree and list regions use roving tabindex, one tab stop each.

MOTION
  reduced       one @media block zeroes animation + transition duration globally.
                Additionally: busy dot stops spinning, sparkline skips its draw-in,
                inspector appears without the slide. Nothing conveys meaning
                through motion alone.
  no autoplay   the log tail auto-scrolls only while `follow` is on, and follow
                turns itself off the moment the user scrolls up.

ANNOUNCEMENTS
  log firehose  aria-live="off". An explicit "announce errors" toggle enables a
                separate aria-live="polite" region carrying errors only.
  toasts        sonner is polite by default; destructive results use role="alert".
  async results NEVER alert()/confirm(). Destructive confirms are <AlertDialog>.
                (mcphub ActivityPage uses window.confirm/alert.)

768px — EVERYTHING BELOW MUST HOLD
  - no horizontal page scroll at any width from 320px up
  - nav rail -> left Sheet from a labelled hamburger; inspector -> right Sheet
  - tables shed to 3 columns (status, identifier, one metric); the rest moves into
    the inspector. Columns are dropped, never squeezed.
  - hover-only affordances are BANNED below 1024px: row actions and the <Id> copy
    button render at opacity-100 via max-lg:opacity-100
  - command palette goes full-screen (h-dvh, no rounding)
  - every target >=24x24; primary actions >=32px tall
  - the shortcut cheatsheet states that chords need a hardware keyboard

OTHER
  prefers-contrast: more   -> --line becomes --line-strong (2 lines, free)
  forced-colors            -> untested. ponytail: add a @media (forced-colors)
                              block if a Windows high-contrast user reports it.
  logical properties       -> padding-inline / border-inline used throughout so a
                              future RTL locale is a dir="rtl" attribute, not a rewrite.

deferred.item: Font subsetting by unicode-range (Latin-only slice of the two variable woff2 files, ~110 KB today)
deferred.add_when: Lighthouse flags font payload, or a deployment reports slow cold loads over a constrained link

deferred.item: Storybook + a visual-regression snapshot of the 6 bespoke components in both themes
deferred.add_when: A second person starts editing `src/ui/`, or the first "it looked fine locally" regression ships

deferred.item: `@tanstack/react-virtual` for the log tail and activity table
deferred.add_when: A list exceeds ~2000 rows in practice; native scroll was kept (D8) precisely so this is a one-component change

deferred.item: Density toggle (compact 28px rows / comfortable 36px) as a `data-density` attribute swapping `--spacing-row`
deferred.add_when: Someone running a 4K display asks, or an accessibility review asks for larger targets
Reported. `prefers-contrast: more` and the glyph-per-status rule already cover most of the need

deferred.item: i18n / RTL. Logical properties are already used throughout, so the groundwork is done
deferred.add_when: A non-English locale is actually requested — not before

risks: `font-display: optional` means a cold first visit paints in the fallback stack. Mitigated because the fallback is also mono for identifiers; the alternative (`swap`) trades this for a guaranteed visible FOUT.

`color-mix(in oklab, …)` powers the `.tint-*` badges and the selection color. Baseline-available since 2023, but a very old kiosk browser degrades to no background rather than a wrong one — acceptable failure direction.

The ESLint identifier rule keys off property NAMES, so a field the data agent calls `label` or `slug` slips through. The regex is one line to extend; a contract review with the data agent at Phase 1 close is the real mitigation.

`@theme inline` means shadcn's `--accent` is our neutral hover surface, not the brand. Anyone copy-pasting a shadcn snippet expecting `bg-accent` to be branded gets a neutral block. Documented at the top of theme.css; a code comment is the only cheap defence.

The docked inspector is deliberately not focus-trapped, which is correct for a non-modal region but differs from the Sheet below 1280px. A screen-reader user resizing across the breakpoint sees the interaction model change. Announced via the region's aria-label; no better fix exists that keeps the page usable.
security: `<Id kind="key">` renders a masked prefix only (`mcpr_…a1f3`). The full API key value is displayed exactly once, at creation, by the keys screen — never in a table, a log line, a tooltip, a `title` attribute or a palette entry. The component has no code path that renders a full key.

`<LogLine>` and every tool/server description render upstream-controlled text as React text nodes. `react/no-danger` is an ESLint error and no markdown renderer is installed — a tool description from a hostile upstream MCP server cannot become markup, a link, or an image beacon.

ANSI escape sequences from piped stdio stderr are stripped by one regex in `Id` and `LogLine` rather than translated by an ansi-to-html library. Removing the parser removes the attack surface it would have added.

Upstream-controlled strings are truncated to 512 chars before reaching any `title` or `aria-label`, so a 2 MB tool name cannot produce a browser-hanging tooltip or an unbounded accessibility-tree node.

Clipboard uses `navigator.clipboard` under `window.isSecureContext` first; the `execCommand` fallback creates and immediately removes a `readOnly`, opacity-0, fixed-position textarea and never leaves it in the DOM. Marked with its ceiling.

No inline `<script>` in index.html (D9), so the CSP can stay `script-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'` with no hash plumbing. Fonts are same-origin, so `font-src 'self'` needs no CDN allowance.
No external stylesheet or font CDN. Everything is bundled by Vite, so there is no third-party origin that can alter the console's rendering or observe its users.

The inspector target is `"<entity>:<id>"` parsed by an exhaustive switch over a closed union — an unknown entity renders a not-found state, never a dynamic import or a route constructed from the param.
